transcription.tex: Use vectors to represent motion. Can we use the \(suvat\) equations with constant acceleration? What changes when acceleration varies with time \(t\)?

\textbf{1. Vector equations for motion}\par A particle has velocity\[\mathbf v=(1-2t)\mathbf i+(3t-3)\mathbf j\quad\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.\]Find (a) its speed at \(t=0\); (b) its bearing at \(t=2\); (c) when it moves (i) parallel to \(\mathbf j\), (ii) parallel to \(-\mathbf i-3\mathbf j\). (3, 2, 6 marks)

\textbf{2. Variable acceleration with vectors}\par A particle \(P\), mass \(0.8\,\mathrm{kg}\), is acted on by a single force \(\mathbf F\). Its position relative to fixed origin \(O\) is\[\mathbf r=2t^3\mathbf i+50t^{-1/2}\mathbf j\quad\mathrm m,\quad t>0.\]Find (a) its speed at \(t=4\); (b) acceleration as a vector at \(t=2\); (c) \(\mathbf F\) at \(t=2\).

\textbf{3. Integration for velocity/displacement}\par A particle moving in a plane has velocity\[\mathbf v=3t\mathbf i+\tfrac12t^2\mathbf j\quad\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}},\quad t\geq0.\]At \(t=0\), its position relative to \(O\) is \((2\mathbf i-3\mathbf j)\,\mathrm m\). Find its position vector at time \(t\).

transcription.tex: Initially, the ball is at the position vector \(\left(\begin{matrix}3\\1\end{matrix}\right)\). Each second, it moves \(\left(\begin{matrix}4\\2\end{matrix}\right)\), i.e. his velocity.\par Where will he be after 1 second?\par After 2 seconds?
After 1 second:\[\binom31+\binom42=\binom73\,\mathrm m.\]
After 2 seconds:\[\binom31+2\binom42=\binom{11}5\,\mathrm m.\]
In general, where is the ball after t seconds?
Add \(t\) lots of \(\binom42\) to \(\binom31\):\[\binom31+t\binom42=\binom{3+4t}{1+2t}.\]
\textbf{Position vector}\[\mathbf r=\mathbf r_0+\mathbf vt,\]where \(\mathbf r_0\) is initial position and \(\mathbf v\) is constant velocity.

transcription.tex: A particle starts at \((3\mathbf i+7\mathbf j)\,\mathrm m\), moving with constant velocity \((2\mathbf i-\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).\par (a) Find its position vector 4 seconds later.\par (b) Find when it is due east of the origin.
\[\mathbf r=\binom37+4\binom2{-1}=\binom{11}3\,\mathrm m.\]

Due east means the \(\mathbf j\) component is zero and the \(\mathbf i\) component is positive:\[\mathbf r=\binom37+t\binom2{-1}=\binom{3+2t}{7-t}.\]\[7-t=0\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=7\,\mathrm s.\]The east component is then \(17\,\mathrm m>0\).
Column vectors may be easier to manipulate than i and j notation; either may be used.

transcription.tex: Some \(suvat\) equations work with vectors. Here \(\mathbf r\) denotes displacement from the initial position:\[\mathbf r=\mathbf ut+\tfrac12\mathbf at^2,\qquad\mathbf v=\mathbf u+\mathbf at.\]Which quantities are vectors, and which are scalars?
\(\mathbf r\): vector.
\(\mathbf u\): vector.
\(\mathbf v\): vector.
\(\mathbf a\): vector.
\(t\): scalar. The scalar formula \(v^2=u^2+2as\) cannot be used by simply squaring vector symbols.

A particle has initial velocity \((-3\mathbf i+\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and constant acceleration \((2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Find (a) its speed and (b) its bearing at \(t=3\,\mathrm s\).

\[\mathbf v=\mathbf u+\mathbf at\]\[=\binom{-3}1+3\binom23=\binom3{10}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.\]\[\text{Speed}=\sqrt{3^2+10^2}=10.4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\quad(3\text{ s.f.}).\]Speed is the scalar magnitude of velocity.
\[\tan\theta=\frac3{10}\Rightarrow\theta=16.7^\circ.\]The bearing is \(017^\circ\). The velocity vector gives the direction of motion; draw it to establish the angle.

transcription.tex: An ice skater is at fixed point \(O\) at \(t=0\), with velocity \((2.4\mathbf i-0.6\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). At \(t=20\,\mathrm s\), velocity is \((-5.6\mathbf i+3.4\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Model the skater as a particle with constant acceleration. Find (a) acceleration; (b) position \(\mathbf s\) relative to \(O\) at time \(t\); (c) when directly north-east of \(O\). A second skater has position \(\mathbf r=(1.1t-6)\mathbf j\,\mathrm m\). (d) Show that they meet.
\[\mathbf v=\mathbf u+\mathbf at\]\[\binom{-5.6}{3.4}=\binom{2.4}{-0.6}+20\mathbf a\]\[20\mathbf a=\binom{-8}4\]\[\mathbf a=\binom{-0.4}{0.2}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}.\]
\[\mathbf s=\mathbf ut+\tfrac12\mathbf at^2\]\[=\binom{2.4}{-0.6}t+\tfrac12\binom{-0.4}{0.2}t^2\]\[=\binom{2.4t-0.2t^2}{-0.6t+0.1t^2}\,\mathrm m.\]

North-east: equal positive components.\[2.4t-0.2t^2=-0.6t+0.1t^2\]\[3t(1-0.1t)=0\]\[t=0\quad\text{or}\quad t=10.\]Reject \(t=0\), at the origin. At \(t=10\), both components are 4, so the time is \(10\,\mathrm s\).

Meeting requires equal position vectors:\[\binom{2.4t-0.2t^2}{-0.6t+0.1t^2}=\binom0{1.1t-6}.\]\[2.4t-0.2t^2=0\]\[0.2t(12-t)=0\Rightarrow t=0\text{ or }12.\]At \(t=0\), north components are \(0\) and \(-6\): no meeting. At \(t=12\):\[-0.6(12)+0.1(12^2)=7.2,\]\[1.1(12)-6=7.2.\]They meet at \(t=12\,\mathrm s\).

transcription.tex: [In this question $\mathbf i$ and $\mathbf j$ are horizontal unit vectors due east and due north respectively. Position vectors are given with respect to a fixed origin $O$.]\par A ship $S$ is moving with constant velocity $(3\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$. At time $t=0$, the position vector of $S$ is $(-4\mathbf i+2\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{km}$.\par (a) Find the position vector of $S$ at time $t$ hours. (2)\par A ship $T$ is moving with constant velocity $(-2\mathbf i+n\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$. At time $t=0$, the position vector of $T$ is $(6\mathbf i+\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{km}$. The two ships meet at the point $P$.\par (b) Find the value of $n$. (5)\par (c) Find the distance $OP$. (4)
\[\mathbf r=\mathbf r_0+\mathbf vt\]\[=(-4\mathbf i+2\mathbf j)+(3\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)t\]\[=(-4+3t)\mathbf i+(2+3t)\mathbf j.\]

For ship \(T\):\[\mathbf r_T=(6\mathbf i+\mathbf j)+(-2\mathbf i+n\mathbf j)t\]\[=(6-2t)\mathbf i+(1+nt)\mathbf j.\]At meeting, positions are identical:\[-4+3t=6-2t\]\[5t=10\Rightarrow t=2.\]\[2+3(2)=1+2n\Rightarrow n=3.5.\]
At \(t=2\), position of \(P\):\[(-4+6)\mathbf i+(2+6)\mathbf j=2\mathbf i+8\mathbf j.\]\[OP=\sqrt{2^2+8^2}\]\[=\sqrt{68}=8.25\,\mathrm{km}\]\[(3\text{ s.f.}).\]

transcription.tex: Question 10

A model boat moves with constant acceleration $(0.2\mathbf i+0.6\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. After 20 seconds its velocity is $(4\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Find the displacement vector of the boat from its starting position after 20 seconds.

\(\mathbf v=4\mathbf i+3\mathbf j,\ t=20,\ \mathbf a=0.2\mathbf i+0.6\mathbf j\). Find \(\mathbf s\):\[\mathbf s=\mathbf vt-\tfrac12\mathbf at^2\]\[=20(4\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)-\frac{20^2}2(0.2\mathbf i+0.6\mathbf j)\]\[=80\mathbf i+60\mathbf j-40\mathbf i-120\mathbf j\]\[=40\mathbf i-60\mathbf j.\]After 20 seconds, displacement is \((40\mathbf i-60\mathbf j)\,\mathrm m\).

transcription.tex: Question 11

A particle $A$ starts at the point with position vector $12\mathbf i+12\mathbf j$. The initial velocity of $A$ is $(-\mathbf i+\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and it has constant acceleration $(2\mathbf i-4\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Another particle, $B$, has initial velocity $\mathbf i\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and constant acceleration $2\mathbf j\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. After 3 seconds the two particles collide. Find:\par a the speeds of the two particles when they collide\par b the position vector of the point where the two particles collide\par c the position vector of $B$’s starting point.

(a) Use \(\mathbf v=\mathbf u+\mathbf at\), \(t=3\). For \(A\):\[\mathbf v=(-\mathbf i+\mathbf j)+3(2\mathbf i-4\mathbf j)\]\[=(-1+6)\mathbf i+(1-12)\mathbf j\]\[=5\mathbf i-11\mathbf j.\]\[|\mathbf v|=\sqrt{5^2+11^2}\]\[=\sqrt{25+121}=\sqrt{146}\]\[=12.1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\quad(3\text{ s.f.}).\]For \(B\):\[\mathbf v=\mathbf i+3(2\mathbf j)=\mathbf i+6\mathbf j\]\[|\mathbf v|=\sqrt{1^2+6^2}\]\[=\sqrt{1+36}=\sqrt{37}\]\[=6.08\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\quad(3\text{ s.f.}).\]

(b) For \(A\), \(\mathbf s=\mathbf ut+\tfrac12\mathbf at^2\):\[\mathbf s=3(-\mathbf i+\mathbf j)+\tfrac12(2\mathbf i-4\mathbf j)9\]\[=-3\mathbf i+3\mathbf j+9\mathbf i-18\mathbf j\]\[=6\mathbf i-15\mathbf j.\]At collision:\[\mathbf r=\mathbf r_0+\mathbf s\]\[=(12\mathbf i+12\mathbf j)+(6\mathbf i-15\mathbf j)\]\[=18\mathbf i-3\mathbf j\,\mathrm m.\]

(c) First find \(B\)’s displacement:\[\mathbf s=\mathbf ut+\tfrac12\mathbf at^2\]\[=3\mathbf i+\tfrac12(2\mathbf j)9\]\[=3\mathbf i+9\mathbf j.\]\(\text{Initial position =}\)\par \(\text{final position}-\text{displacement:}\)\[\mathbf r_0=\mathbf r-\mathbf s\]\[=(18\mathbf i-3\mathbf j)-(3\mathbf i+9\mathbf j)\]\[=15\mathbf i-12\mathbf j\,\mathrm m.\]

transcription.tex: Question 12

A ship is moving such that at time 12:00 its position is $O$ and its velocity is $(-4\mathbf i+8\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$. At 14:00, the ship is travelling with velocity $(-2\mathbf i-6\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$.\par Relative to $O$, the ship has displacement $\mathbf s$ at time $t$ hours after 12:00 where $t\geq0$. Modelling the ship as a particle with constant acceleration, find:\par a the acceleration of the ship\par b an expression for $\mathbf s$ in terms of $t$\par c the time at which the ship is directly south-west of $O$.\par At time $t$ hours after 12:00, another ship has displacement $\mathbf r=(40-25t)\mathbf j$ relative to $O$.\par (d) Find the position vector of the point where the two ships meet.

(a) \(\mathbf u=-4\mathbf i+8\mathbf j,\ \mathbf v=-2\mathbf i-6\mathbf j,\ t=2\).\[\mathbf v=\mathbf u+\mathbf at\]\[-2\mathbf i-6\mathbf j=-4\mathbf i+8\mathbf j+2\mathbf a\]\[2\mathbf a=2\mathbf i-14\mathbf j\]\[\mathbf a=\mathbf i-7\mathbf j\quad\mathrm{km\,h^{-2}}.\]
(b) \[\mathbf s=\mathbf ut+\tfrac12\mathbf at^2\]\[=(-4\mathbf i+8\mathbf j)t+\tfrac12(\mathbf i-7\mathbf j)t^2\]\[=(-4t+0.5t^2)\mathbf i+(8t-3.5t^2)\mathbf j\,\mathrm{km}.\]

(c) South-west means equal negative components:\[-4t+0.5t^2=8t-3.5t^2\]\[4t^2=12t\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=0\text{ or }3.\]Reject \(t=0\), at \(O\). At \(t=3\), both components are \(-7.5\). This is 3 hours after 12:00, at 15:00.

(d) At meeting, \(\mathbf r=\mathbf s\). As \(\mathbf r\) has no \(\mathbf i\) component:\[-4t+0.5t^2=0\Rightarrow0.5t^2=4t\Rightarrow t=0\text{ or }8.\]At \(t=0\), positions differ: \(0\ne40\mathbf j\). At \(t=8\):\[\mathbf r=(40-25\times8)\mathbf j=-160\mathbf j,\]\[8(8)-3.5(8^2)=-160.\]They meet 160 km south of \(O\), at position \(-160\mathbf j\,\mathrm{km}\).

transcription.tex: At an air show, an aeroplane passes over a control tower with velocity \((20\mathbf i-100\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), flying horizontally with constant acceleration \(6\mathbf j\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). A second plane passes the tower \(t>0\) seconds later, with velocity \((70\mathbf i+40\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), in a higher horizontal plane with acceleration \(-8\mathbf j\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). They subsequently pass directly over one another. Find \(t\).

Let the horizontal position at crossing be \(\mathbf r\), and let \(T\) be time since the first plane passed the tower. For the first plane:\[\mathbf u=\binom{20}{-100},\quad\mathbf a=\binom06.\]\[\mathbf r=\mathbf uT+\tfrac12\mathbf aT^2\]\[=\binom{20}{-100}T+\frac{T^2}2\binom06\]\[=\binom{20T}{-100T+3T^2}.\]For the second plane, elapsed time is \(T-t\):\[\mathbf r=\binom{70}{40}(T-t)+\frac{(T-t)^2}2\binom0{-8}\]\[=\binom{70T-70t}{40T-40t-4T^2-4t^2+8Tt}.\]

Equate east components:\[20T=70T-70t\]\[70T-20T=70t\quad\Rightarrow\quad T=\frac75t.\]Equate north components:\[-100T+3T^2=40T-40t-4T^2-4t^2+8Tt\]\[7T^2+4t^2-8Tt=140T-40t.\]Substitute \(T=7t/5\):\[\frac{7\times7^2}{25}t^2+4t^2-\frac{8\times7}5t^2\]\[=\frac{140\times7}5t-40t.\]\[\left(\frac{343}{25}+4-\frac{56}5\right)t^2=(196-40)t\]\[\frac{163}{25}t^2=156t.\]As \(t>0\):\[t=\frac{3900}{163}=23.926\ldots\,\mathrm s\]\[=24\,\mathrm s\quad(2\text{ s.f.}).\]

transcription.tex: A velocity vector gives both direction and magnitude, so can represent projection and subsequent motion.\par A racket strikes a ball at \(A\), position \(20\mathbf j\,\mathrm m\) relative to \(O\). Initial velocity is \((5\mathbf i+8\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), with \(\mathbf i\) horizontal and \(\mathbf j\) upward. It moves freely under gravity until hitting horizontal ground at \(B\). Find (a) speed after 1.5 seconds; (b) position \(\mathbf r(t)\) relative to \(O\); (c) \(OB\).

\[\mathbf v=\mathbf u+\mathbf at\]\[=\binom58+\binom0{-9.8}t\]\[=\binom5{8-9.8t}.\]At \(t=1.5\):\[\mathbf v=\binom5{-6.7}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.\]\[|\mathbf v|=\sqrt{5^2+6.7^2}\]\[=8.4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\]\[(2\text{ s.f.}).\]

Displacement relative to \(A\):\[\mathbf r_A=\mathbf ut+\tfrac12\mathbf at^2\]\[=\binom58t+\tfrac12\binom0{-9.8}t^2\]\[=\binom{5t}{8t-4.9t^2}.\]Position relative to \(O\):\[\mathbf r=\binom0{20}+\binom{5t}{8t-4.9t^2}\]\[=\binom{5t}{8t-4.9t^2+20}\,\mathrm m.\]
At ground level, north/up component is zero:\[8t-4.9t^2+20=0.\]Positive root \(t=2.995\ldots\,\mathrm s\). Horizontal component gives\[OB=5t=15\,\mathrm m\quad(2\text{ s.f.}).\]

transcription.tex: [In this question, the unit vectors $\mathbf i$ and $\mathbf j$ are horizontal and vertical respectively.]\par The point $O$ is a fixed point on a horizontal plane. A ball is projected from $O$ with velocity $(6\mathbf i+12\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and passes through the point $A$ at time $t$ seconds after projection. The point $B$ is on the horizontal plane vertically below $A$, as shown in Figure 3. It is given that $OB=2AB$. Find\par (a) the value of $t$, (7)\par (b) the speed, $V\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, of the ball at the instant when it passes through $A$. (5)\par At another point $C$ on the path the speed of the ball is also $V\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.\par (c) Find the time taken for the ball to travel from $O$ to $C$. (3)
Horizontal distance: \(6t\). Vertical height: \(12t-\tfrac12gt^2\).\[2(12t-\tfrac12gt^2)=6t\]\[(24-6)t=gt^2.\]As \(t>0\):\[18=gt\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=\frac{18}g=1.84\,\mathrm s.\]
Horizontal velocity is 6. At \(A\), vertical velocity:\[12-gt=12-18=-6.\]Thus\[V=\sqrt{6^2+(-6)^2}=\sqrt{72}=6\sqrt2\]\[=8.49\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.\]
At the other point with this speed, vertical velocity is \(+6\):\[12-gt=6\]\[\Rightarrow t=\frac6g=0.61\,\mathrm s.\]

transcription.tex: Question 3

A ball is projected from a point $A$ at the top of a cliff, with position vector $25\mathbf j\,\mathrm m$ relative to the base of the cliff $O$. The base of the cliff is at sea level. The velocity of projection is $(3p\mathbf i+p\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, where $p$ is a constant. After 2 seconds, the ball passes a point $B$ with position vector $(q\mathbf i+10\mathbf j)\,\mathrm m$, where $q$ is a constant, before hitting the sea at point $C$. The ball is modelled as a particle moving freely under gravity and the sea is modelled as a horizontal plane.\par Find the velocity vector of the ball at point $B$.

\(\mathbf u=3p\mathbf i+p\mathbf j,\ \mathbf a=-9.8\mathbf j,\ t=2\).\[\mathbf v=\mathbf u+\mathbf at\]\[=\binom{3p}p+2\binom0{-9.8}=\binom{3p}{p-19.6}.\quad(1)\]Also, \(\mathbf r_0=25\mathbf j\), \(\mathbf r=q\mathbf i+10\mathbf j\):\[\mathbf s=\mathbf r-\mathbf r_0\]\[=q\mathbf i+10\mathbf j-25\mathbf j=q\mathbf i-15\mathbf j.\]

\[\mathbf s=\mathbf ut+\tfrac12\mathbf at^2\]\[\binom q{-15}=2\binom{3p}p+\frac{2^2}2\binom0{-9.8}.\]Compare vertical components:\[-15=2p-19.6\]\[2p=19.6-15\quad\Rightarrow\quad p=\frac{4.6}2=2.3.\]Substitute in (1):\[\mathbf v=\binom{3\times2.3}{2.3-19.6}=\binom{6.9}{-17.3}.\]Velocity at \(B\) is \((6.9\mathbf i-17\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), components to 2 s.f.

transcription.tex: Question 4

A particle $P$ is projected with velocity $(3u\mathbf i+4u\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ from a fixed point $O$ on horizontal ground. Given that $P$ strikes the ground at a point 750 m from $O$,\par a show that $u=17.5$\par b calculate the greatest height above the ground reached by $P$\par c find the angle the direction of motion of $P$ makes with $\mathbf i$ when $t=5$.

(a) \(\mathbf u=3u\mathbf i+4u\mathbf j,\ \mathbf a=-9.8\mathbf j,\ \mathbf s=750\mathbf i\).\[\mathbf s=\mathbf ut+\tfrac12\mathbf at^2\]\[750\mathbf i=(3u\mathbf i+4u\mathbf j)t+\tfrac12(-9.8\mathbf j)t^2\]\[=3ut\mathbf i+(4ut-4.9t^2)\mathbf j.\]Horizontal components:\[750=3ut\Rightarrow t=\frac{250}u.\]Vertical components:\[0=4ut-4.9t^2\]\[0=\frac{4u\times250}u-4.9\left(\frac{250}u\right)^2\]\[=1000-\frac{306250}{u^2}\]\[u^2=\frac{306250}{1000}=306.25\]\[u=\sqrt{306.25}=17.5.\]
(b) At greatest height, vertical velocity is zero. Vertically, \(u_y=4u=70\), \(a=-9.8\), \(v_y=0\).\[v_y^2=u_y^2+2as\]\[0=70^2-2(9.8)s\]\[s=\frac{70^2}{2\times9.8}=250\,\mathrm m.\]

(c) At \(t=5\),\[\mathbf v=\mathbf u+\mathbf at\]\[=(52.5\mathbf i+70\mathbf j)-5(9.8\mathbf j)\]\[=52.5\mathbf i+21\mathbf j.\]\[\tan\theta=\frac{v_y}{v_x}=\frac{21}{52.5}=0.4\]\[\theta=21.8^\circ\approx22^\circ\quad(2\text{ s.f.}),\]above the horizontal.

transcription.tex: Question 5

A particle is projected with velocity $(8\mathbf i+10\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ from a point $O$ at the top of a cliff and moves freely under gravity. Six seconds after projection, the particle strikes the sea at the point $S$. Calculate:\par a the horizontal distance between $O$ and $S$\par b the vertical distance between $O$ and $S$.\par At time $T$ seconds after projection, the particle is moving with velocity $(8\mathbf i-14.5\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.\par (c) Find the value of $T$ and the position vector, relative to $O$, of the particle at this instant.
(a) Let position of \(S\) be \(x\mathbf i+y\mathbf j\). Horizontal motion:\[x=u_xt=8\times6=48\,\mathrm m.\]
(b) Vertical motion:\[y=u_yt+\tfrac12at^2\]\[=10\times6-4.9\times6^2=-116.4\,\mathrm m.\]The vertical distance is 120 m (2 s.f.), downwards.

(c) \[\mathbf v=\mathbf u+\mathbf aT\]\[8\mathbf i-14.5\mathbf j=(8\mathbf i+10\mathbf j)-9.8T\mathbf j.\]Compare vertical components:\[-14.5=10-9.8T\]\[T=\frac{24.5}{9.8}=\frac52=2.5\,\mathrm s.\]Then\[\mathbf s=\mathbf uT+\tfrac12\mathbf aT^2\]\[=\tfrac52(8\mathbf i+10\mathbf j)+\tfrac12(-9.8\mathbf j)(\tfrac52)^2\]\[=(8\times\tfrac52)\mathbf i+\left(10\times\tfrac52-4.9(\tfrac52)^2\right)\mathbf j\]\[=\left(20\mathbf i-\frac{45}8\mathbf j\right)\,\mathrm m.\]

transcription.tex: Question 6

In this question use $g=10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.\par A body $B$ is projected from a fixed point $O$ on horizontal ground with velocity $(a\mathbf i+b\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, where $a$ and $b$ are positive constants. The body moves freely under gravity until it hits the ground at the point $P$, where it immediately comes to rest.\par The position vector of a point on the path of $B$ relative to $O$ is $(x\mathbf i+y\mathbf j)\,\mathrm m$.\par (a) Show that $y=\frac{bx}{a}-\frac{5x^2}{a^2}$.\par Given that $a=8$, $OP=X$ m and the maximum vertical height of $B$ above the ground is $Y$ m,\par b find, in terms of $b$,   i $X$     ii $Y$.

(a) \[\mathbf s=\mathbf ut+\tfrac12\mathbf at^2\]\[x\mathbf i+y\mathbf j=(a\mathbf i+b\mathbf j)t+\tfrac12(-10\mathbf j)t^2.\]Horizontal components:\[x=at\Rightarrow t=\frac xa.\quad(1)\]Vertical components:\[y=bt-5t^2.\quad(2)\]Substitute (1) in (2):\[y=\frac{bx}a-\frac{5x^2}{a^2},\]as required.
b.i At landing, \(x=X,y=0,a=8\):\[0=\frac{bX}8-\frac{5X^2}{64}\]\[\frac{5X^2}{64}=\frac{bX}8\Rightarrow5X^2=8bX.\]Reject \(X=0\):\[X=\frac{8b}5=1.6b.\]
b.ii Maximum height occurs halfway along the range:\[x=\frac X2=\frac{4b}5.\]\[Y=\frac{b\times4b}{8\times5}-\frac{5(4b)^2}{64\times5^2}\]\[=\frac{b^2}{10}-\frac{b^2}{20}=\frac{b^2}{20}=0.05b^2.\]

transcription.tex: \[s\ \xrightarrow{\ d/dt\ }\ v\ \xrightarrow{\ d/dt\ }\ a\]\[s\ \xleftarrow{\ \int v\,dt\ }\ v\ \xleftarrow{\ \int a\,dt\ }\ a\]

In Mechanics Year 1, velocity is rate of change of displacement and acceleration is rate of change of velocity:\[v=\frac{ds}{dt},\qquad a=\frac{dv}{dt}.\]Reverse by integration: \(v=\int a\,dt\), \(s=\int v\,dt\), with constants found from initial conditions. Stay in one dimension, now using more complex Pure Year 2 functions.

A particle is moving in a straight line with acceleration at time \(t\) seconds given by\par \(a=\cos 2\pi t \mathrm{m}{\mathrm{s}}^{-2},\hspace{1.12em}t\ge 0\)\par The velocity of the particle at time \(t=0\) is \(\frac{1}{2\pi }\) ms-1. Find:\par (a) an expression for the velocity at time \(t\) seconds\par (b) the maximum speed\par (c) the distance travelled in the first 3 seconds.
\[v=\int\cos(2\pi t)\,dt\]\[=\frac1{2\pi}\sin(2\pi t)+c.\]Reverse chain rule: divide by the constant multiplying \(t\). At \(t=0\):\[v=0+c=\frac1{2\pi}.\]\[v=\frac1{2\pi}\bigl(\sin(2\pi t)+1\bigr).\]
Maximum sine value is 1:\[v_{\max}=\frac1{2\pi}+\frac1{2\pi}=\frac1\pi\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.\]Velocity is nonnegative, so this is also maximum speed.

Area under the velocity–time graph gives distance because \(v\geq0\). Factor out \(1/(2\pi)\):\[s=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^3(\sin(2\pi t)+1)\,dt\]\[=\frac1{2\pi}\left[-\frac1{2\pi}\cos(2\pi t)+t\right]_0^3\]\[=\frac3{2\pi}=0.477\,\mathrm m\quad(3\text{ s.f.}).\]

transcription.tex: Question 7

A particle moves in a straight line. At time $t$ seconds after it begins its motion, the acceleration of the particle is $3\sqrt t\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ where $t>0$. Given that after 1 second the particle is moving with velocity $2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, find the time taken for the particle to travel 16 m.

Integrate twice to obtain displacement, then find when 16 m has been travelled.\[v=\int a\,dt=\int3\sqrt t\,dt\]\[=3\times\frac23t^{3/2}+c=2t^{3/2}+c.\]Use \(t=1,v=2\):\[2=2(1^{3/2})+c\Rightarrow c=0.\]\[v=2t^{3/2}.\]

\[s=\int v\,dt=\int2t^{3/2}\,dt\]\[=\frac25\times2t^{5/2}+c_2=\frac45t^{5/2}+c_2.\]Measure displacement from the starting position, so \(s(0)=0\) gives \(c_2=0\). Since \(v\geq0\), distance equals displacement:\[16=\frac45t^{5/2}\]\[20=t^{5/2}\Rightarrow t=20^{2/5}=3.3144\ldots.\]It takes \(3.31\,\mathrm s\) (3 s.f.).

transcription.tex: Question 8

A runner takes part in a race in which competitors have to sprint 200 m in a straight line. At time $t$ seconds after starting, her displacement, $s$, from the starting position is modelled as:\par $s=k\sqrt t$, $0\leq t\leq T$.\par Given that the runner completes the race in 25 seconds,\par a find the value of $k$ and the value of $T$\par b find the speed of the runner when she crosses the finish line\par c criticise this model for small values of $t$.
(a) At the finish \(s=200,t=25\), so \(T=25\,\mathrm s\).\[200=k\sqrt{25}\quad\Rightarrow\quad k=\frac{200}5=40.\]

(c) For small positive \(t\), predicted speed is unrealistically large. For example, at \(t=0.01\,\mathrm s\):\[v=20(0.01)^{-1/2}=200\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.\]No human can run this fast; the model is unsuitable near the start.

transcription.tex: Question 9

A particle is moving in a straight line. At time $t$ seconds, where $t\geq0$, the acceleration of $P$ is $a\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ and the velocity $v\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ of $P$ is given by $v=2+8\sin kt$ where $k$ is a constant.\par The initial acceleration of $P$ is $4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.\par (a) Find the value of $k$.\par Using the value of $k$ found in part a,\par b find, in terms of $\pi$, the values of $t$ in the interval $0\le t\le4\pi$ for which $a=0$\par c show that $4a^2=64-(v-2)^2$\par d find the maximum velocity and the maximum acceleration.
(a) \[a=\frac{dv}{dt}=8k\cos(kt).\]At \(t=0,a=4\):\[4=8k\quad\Rightarrow\quad k=\tfrac12.\]
(b) \[a=8\times\tfrac12\cos(\tfrac12t)=4\cos(\tfrac12t).\]For \(a=0\):\[\cos(\tfrac12t)=0\]\[\tfrac12t=\tfrac\pi2,\tfrac{3\pi}2\Rightarrow t=\pi,3\pi.\]

(d) At a maximum of velocity, \(a=0\). The candidates from (b) are \(\pi,3\pi\):\[\sin(\pi/2)=1,\]\[\sin(3\pi/2)=-1.\]Thus \(v_{\max}=2+8=10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\); the other is a minimum.\par At an interior acceleration extremum, \(da/dt=0\). Since \(a\) is a multiple of cosine, its derivative is a multiple of sine. Thus \(\sin(t/2)=0\), so \(v=2\). From (c):\[4a^2=64-(2-2)^2=64\]\[a=\pm4.\]The maximum is \(+4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\), attained when cosine is 1 (including \(t=0\)).
